messages.speaker: them
messages.text: i've been turning the lisbon offer over all weekend, and i think the money is good but the work is narrower than what i do now. is that a real step back, or do i just like the sound of my current title?

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: narrow is only a step back if the skills don't travel. what's the actual brief?

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: platform reliability for one product line. good team, three strong engineers, and the roadmap i'd inherit is honestly interesting — but i'd stop touching the parts i built last year

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: and does the offer have a path back to breadth, or is narrow the identity of the role

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: they said breadth comes later, quote, when the platform is boring. i find that phrase appealing and also slightly suspicious

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: suspicious is correct. when they say boring, make them define boring in numbers — error budget, on-call load, scope of the mandate

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: that's the question my gut wanted to ask and my politeness wouldn't let it. i'll ask it thursday

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: good. and don't accept thursday's vibe as an answer, make them point at a metric

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: metric-first it is. unrelated: re-reading my notes from our june session, the 'keep your runway boring and your problems interesting' line hasn't aged a day

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: i unironically stand by that one. save it for thursday's notes

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: will do. one more — does anything ever come up about platform engineers moving the other way, from narrow roles back to product teams?

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: constantly. two this year, and both got more out of it than they expected

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: that settles my bias a little. thursday i'll take notes and report back

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: i'm around until six if the call runs long

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: thinking of you this morning. remember: metric, numbers, and ask for a decision date if they dodge it

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: went in early to rehearse in a meeting room. i'll write everything down so thursday-me can't romanticise anything

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: rehearse the awkward pause too

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: the pause is rehearsed. they flinched at the error-budget question, in a good way — the numbers exist, they just never show them to candidates

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: that's a real answer, not a vibe

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: i'll push on the breadth path next week. also they mentioned the team keeps weekly retro docs candidates can read, which felt honest

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: read them. people's internal writing is the real brochure

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: reading them now. the sentiment halfway through is a little tired, but the specifics are all there — incidents with real post-mortems, not theatre

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: tired-but-specific beats polished-and-empty every time

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: last thing today: if they come back tuesday with a sign-by-friday deadline, is that a pressure tactic or normal ops?

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: normal ops unless it's aggressive for no reason. ask what's driving it

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: will do. talk monday

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: decision time. they came back with the numbers, a slightly better title, and no friday ultimatum after all — the retro docs were right, they run on reality rather than theatre

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: and what did the numbers say about breadth

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: if the platform stays unreliable the mandate grows; if it ever becomes boring, i rotate to the security team for a year. written down, with a name attached

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: then it's a real offer with a real floor

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: i told them i'd sign by monday. i feel strangely calm about it, which is probably information too

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: that calm is the signal. celebrate properly, and send me your first retro once you've started

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: deal. and when the first incident lands, i'll send you the post-mortem as a housewarming gift 🙂

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: a retirement gift, more like. proud of you

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: don't make me sentimental at my desk. one practical thing: when you're next in town in october, dinner is on me

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: october it is. i'll bring the good notebook

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: the leather one. bring it, i intend to steal your method for margin notes

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: the leather one, guarded with my life. see you in lisbon's opposite
